findings.diagnosis: The prompt pushes scorers to avoid high-contradiction positions by relocating cuts onto function-word boundaries (splitting determiners, auxiliaries, or list items), which preserves no-contradiction at the cost of much lower cohesion.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_399','en_us_845','en_us_345','en_us_655','en_us_1253','en_us_167'] — each policy set contains a single high-contradiction cut that zeroed the H_set and other kept cuts were shifted to create many tiny function-word fragments or broken enumerations, collapsing overall cohesion.

edit.text: Do not avoid contradiction risk by relocating cuts onto function-word boundaries. Prefer keeping short function words (determiners, auxiliaries, conjunctions) attached to adjacent content words; avoid segmentations that split determiners/auxiliaries from their noun or verb phrases merely to dodge a risky boundary.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt under-emphasizes preserving predicate-argument and noun-phrase integrity: scorers sometimes cut inside verb+object, determiner+noun, or compound-name spans, harming cohesion especially at longer latency bins.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_1024','en_us_1087','en_us_957','en_us_1415','en_us_1179'] — in each target the better segmentation keeps heads with their complements (verb+object, determiner+noun, or full NP titles) and yields much higher H_set than policy which split those spans.

edit.text: Example guidance: prefer cuts that keep verb+object and determiner+noun together; avoid cutting between auxiliaries and their complements or inside long noun phrases or compound names, since those attachments strongly preserve cohesion.
